13.0.0.en: If you have been given the gift of speaking in many of the languages of men, or even if we imagine that you know the language of angels, which of course no one will know until he reaches the Kingdom, without having love, no benefit is achieved and there will be no fruit from this gift; rather you are like hollow words empty of any effect, like loud sounds with no real work. It is love that gives benefit to the gifts.

13.1.0.en: If I am given the gifts of prophesying God’s purposes, and I know the hidden mysteries of God’s will, and if I obtain all the knowledge that it is within a person’s power to obtain, and if I have a high degree of strong faith that enables me to remove mountains, that is, to work powers and miracles... if I have all this but my heart is not full of love, I am nothing. The essential characteristic of the spiritual person is love, not knowledge or the various gifts.

13.2.0.en: If I am prepared to give all my goods to the poor and to give my body to the fire as a witness to the Lord, but these deeds do not proceed from love, then these sacrifices and offerings, although they may benefit others, bring me no benefit and do not achieve the salvation of my soul, because they may be done out of pride or out of embarrassment before others.

13.2.1.en: Examine your words, your thoughts and your deeds in your relationship with others: is it love that moves them, or your personal aims? And when you notice people’s faults and rebuke them, is it with compassion and love, or out of annoyance at their behavior? If you feel love, then act as you wish; and if you do not feel it, withdraw until you first set your heart right, because your works are not acceptable to God.

13.3.0.en: Suffereth long and is kind: when a person’s heart is filled with love for all, he is not hasty to anger, but is long-suffering with offenders and tender toward them until he brings them out of their troubles, and is patient with beginners until they learn wisdom and upright conduct.

13.3.1.en: Love envieth not: love does not feel bitterness and pain when others succeed and are happy; and this is logical, because if love drives us to make others happy, how can we be pained when good comes to them? The one who loves does not think of acquiring for himself what others have, or become vexed at their good things and success, but rejoices and wishes them still more.

13.3.2.en: Love vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up: love makes us respect others and honor them, so that we are not filled with conceit and do not exalt ourselves in relation to others, because we love them and so honor them more than we honor ourselves.

13.4.0.en: Love doth not behave itself unseemly: when the loving person is compelled to reprove something that another has done, he does so with complete calm and in courteous words; he has such sensitivity that he takes care not to hurt the feelings of others even when they have erred, because he sees the beauty in others, while for their shortcomings he finds excuses and tries to help them correct them with gentleness and love.

13.4.1.en: Seeketh not her own: love is the opposite of selfishness and makes a person think of the needs and interests of others before his own; and God, who is loving, pours out more abundant blessings and cares for the person who lays down his life for others. He does not care for himself, but God cares for him.

13.4.2.en: Is not easily provoked: love does not make its possessor flare up in anger so that he protests in a loud voice or raises his hands and curses, or goes on until it comes to fighting and sometimes killing. This is because the loving person does not look at others in a spirit of criticism, seeking to condemn them; on the contrary, love makes him not reckon to others their faults.

13.4.3.en: Thinketh no evil: that is, it is not quick to assume evil intent in others or to accuse them of it, and is content with caution, while finding an excuse for them if their falling into evil is proved.

13.5.0.en: Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth: the world encourages many sins and counts them success and distinction, such as lying and obtaining more than one’s personal rights; but love does not rejoice in people’s evils, but wishes for their salvation and rejoices in their good works, that is, the truth that is in them, which is the work of God that helps them toward virtues and good works.

13.6.0.en: Love beareth all things: the loving person bears the shortcomings of others and their faults against him.

13.6.1.en: Believeth all things: the loving person does not easily believe any evil thing that may be said about others, but simply believes all that is good before him, with caution and prayer, until God reveals how to deal with others, so that he escapes any evil. The loving person does not open his ears to the words of slanderers who seek to devise plots. Likewise love believes all God’s promises and commandments, whatever the surrounding circumstances of life or the conduct of people far from God.

13.6.2.en: Hopeth all things: sincere love never knows despair, expecting the work of God with calm, stillness, patience and hope in Him.

13.6.3.en: Endureth all things: true love is patient; it does not hasten results, and its patience is not quickly exhausted. God, who sees your patience and long-suffering, will give you a just recompense.

13.6.4.en: Truly, how broad is the work of love and its manifestations! And how much I need to review my conduct in the light of this, so that I may know my standing with respect to the Christian love required of me.

13.7.0.en: God is love, and since God is eternal, without beginning or end, love is everlasting and does not pass away, not even after death, although many things become void and come to an end with the end of time, such as prophecies, which are the foretelling of future things; they will end with the completion of salvation in eternity, for they will have no existence then, since they will have been fulfilled. And tongues, that is, the many languages, which are a means of understanding among people during their temporal life, will have no existence in the heavenly glories, where the luminous, glorified bodies will converse by means other than the languages we know.

13.7.1.en: And all the knowledge that a person can acquire in his temporal life will be nothing before the truth that will be revealed to all.

13.8.0.en: What we attain now of knowledge, or prophesy by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, is only a small part of the mysteries of the divine truth.

13.9.0.en: When the sun of the other life rises on us with the perfect truth, we shall not need this partial knowledge, which is like a lamp that is not needed in the light of the sun.

13.10.0.en: The Apostle clarifies here what went before. Just as when a person becomes a man he does not behave in the same manner as when he was a child, whether in speech, in understanding or in thinking, so also in the eternal glory you will reach the perfection of knowledge with which all partial knowledge is done away.

13.11.0.en: This is another illustrative example. We are now in the body, seeing things as through a mirror, that is, we see the image of things and not their reality, so our vision is imperfect. For this reason much of what we know about God remains not entirely clear to us, as though it were a riddle. But in eternity we shall see the things themselves and not their image, that is, in complete clarity and directly.

13.12.0.en: All this change will take place in the other life. But now, while we are still on this earth, the Apostle instructs us to abide in faith, hope and love, for these are the three foundations of the spiritual life. Faith is our trust in eternal life with Christ, but in eternity we shall see and perceive what we lived by faith on earth, and there faith will have no role. Likewise hope will end when the hopes we lived by on earth are fulfilled for us in heaven.

13.12.1.en: Therefore the Apostle exalts the importance of love, for it will never pass away and is always in the heart, on earth and also in heaven; for God is love, and in eternity we do not reach the end of God’s love, but we reach the utmost degree in our comprehension of this love.

13.12.2.en: Examine yourself: is your love toward God growing in greater concern for your prayers and your readings? And your love for others, is it increasing in more self-giving and sacrifices? A natural living being must always grow. So think how you can show love to everyone around you.

14.0.s.en: (1) The gift of speaking in tongues and of prophesying

14.0.0.en: Walk in love, but I also instruct you to strive to acquire the spiritual gifts, especially prophesying, which is teaching others the spiritual truths and interpreting the word of God by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit. It is far better than desiring the gift of praying in tongues, which many of the Corinthians desired; this was not used in teaching but was a kind of personal spiritual devotion in the closet, which no one hears, and he understands what he prays, and under the influence of his submission to the Holy Spirit he speaks truths and mysteries.

14.0.1.en: Perhaps many desired to acquire it as though it were a high spiritual degree, although the gifts, as we have mentioned, are not evidence of a person’s salvation but are given for the benefit of the Church.

14.0.2.en: This teaches us not to covet the gifts of others, but to invest what God has given us for the service of others.

14.1.0.en: But he that prophesieth, that is, teaches others (since prophesying is speaking about the future, and our future in the New Testament is the Kingdom and all the teachings that speak of God’s reign over our hearts and our preparation for eternity), speaks to people in understandable words that help the spiritual edification of the hearers, encourages them to spiritual conduct by preaching, and gladdens them with spiritual consolations (comfort) so that they continue the struggle.

14.2.0.en: Whoever speaks in a tongue in his closet edifies himself as a result of his sense of the Holy Spirit’s working with him, but the benefit of this does not go beyond his own person.

14.2.1.en: By contrast, whoever prophesies helps the spiritual edification of others, and so benefits the members of the Church who hear him.

14.3.0.en: I wish your desires to speak in tongues in prayer to be fulfilled, but I would rather that you seek after the gift of prophesying, because it is greater than the gift of speaking in a tongue in terms of its benefit to the believers; unless it is speaking in one of the known languages of the world, on condition that there is an interpreter so that the hearers may understand, because this language is known in other parts of the world, whereas the hearers need translation in order to understand and benefit spiritually.

14.4.0.en: Now the Apostle takes himself as an example: if he came to them speaking in a language foreign to them, they would not benefit at all; but if he spoke to them in a language they understand, he would declare the truths of the faith that were revealed to him, and also all the spiritual sciences, and they would benefit greatly.

14.4.1.en: It is good that you enjoy prayer and delight in reading the word of God for your benefit. But you also need to be concerned to draw others to God and to teach them in the way suitable for them, so that they may be bound to the Church.

14.4.2.en: Be concerned for the repentance of those around you and for their partaking of the Holy Mysteries.

14.5.0.en: Here the Apostle brings an eloquent example that brings his thought near to the reader of the Epistle. He speaks of things without reason, that is, lifeless things, namely musical instruments that give out sounds, such as the pipe or the harp; if their notes do not give a melody that has meaning, with variety and effect, no one will listen to them, since they will give no benefit to the hearers.

14.6.0.en: The trumpet was used in wars in ancient times as a means of preparing for battle and conveying the commander’s instructions to the soldiers by means of agreed sounds. If the trumpet gave an unclear sound that was not agreed upon, the fighters would not know the commander’s instructions, and this unclear sound would have no useful role in the battle.

14.7.0.en: So it is with you also: if the language in which you speak is not understood by the hearers, they will not know what you mean, and your speech will be of no benefit to them, as though you were speaking into the air.

14.8.0.en: There are a great number of languages in the world, and the words in each have their meaning, but none of them will be of any use to me unless I understand that language; and I will not benefit at all from listening to a speaker whose language I do not know, and he likewise will understand nothing if I speak to him in a language that he does not know.

14.9.0.en: You also, since you strive earnestly to obtain spiritual gifts, ask that there be increased to you what is useful and good for the edification of others in the Church.

14.10.0.en: For whoever speaks in a language that the hearers do not understand will not benefit the Church in anything unless it is interpreted so as to become understood.

14.10.1.en: Therefore whoever receives the gift of speaking in tongues should ask God to prepare someone to interpret what he says for the benefit of the hearers, whether the interpreter is the speaker himself or another person; for this is a gift given so that he may speak with it when he goes to preach in a place where they understand only this language. But among his brethren who do not understand this foreign language, an interpreter is required, and otherwise let him keep silent, as the rest of this chapter affirms.

14.10.2.en: Be concerned to speak words suited to whoever hears you, not only simplified for the simple and for children, but suited to the nature, work and interests of the hearers, so that they come to hear you with eagerness and you are able to show them Christ through your speech.

14.11.0.en: It is not only that if I address people in a language they do not understand it does not benefit them, but also if I pray in a language other than my own and not understood, I feel the refreshing of the spirit, but I do not understand with my mind what I say, and my mind does not take part in the prayer.

14.12.0.en: St. Paul asks what is the duty toward the Holy Spirit’s gift to me of speaking in a tongue. He answers, saying that he must interpret what he says in this foreign language, and if he does not know how to interpret, let another interpret, one of those who have received the gift of interpretation. Likewise also when he chants in a language foreign to the hearers, he must understand with his mind what he chants, to enjoy the prayer and chanting more; otherwise there is no need to pray or chant in a foreign language that he can interpret neither for himself nor for others.

14.13.0.en: Otherwise the unlearned, that is, the one who does not know the language, who hears me when I pray in a language not interpreted for him, does not know when to say Amen when I give thanks to God, because he does not understand me, and there is no participation in the prayer.

14.14.0.en: You give thanks to God, and that is good, but the other, who understands nothing of what you pray, what benefit has he from your prayer? He gains nothing from it.

14.15.0.en: I thank my God that I speak with more tongues than any of you, but when I am in the Church I would rather speak five words that I can make understood by others, so that I teach them, than speak many words in a language that no one understands.

14.16.0.en: Therefore I instruct you to be like children in simplicity and innocence, but do not behave as if you were children in your thinking, unable to think seriously and deeply. That is, the Apostle wishes to stress the importance of understanding and perceiving spiritual things, and that the ability to build up the Church spiritually be the chief aim, and that speaking in a tongue not be the aim.

14.16.1.en: Truly, let us distinguish in our life between what is essential and what is additional.

14.16.2.en: If you are a servant, may you take care, when you lead others in prayer or chanting or when preaching, that it be in a way that encourages those present to take part, and that you not go alone in prayer and chanting at a speed that others cannot keep up with, or in tunes that most of those with you cannot manage; for the life of the Church is founded on fellowship among the believers.

14.17.0.en: The Apostle quoted the saying that appears in (Isa 28:11, 12), when He told His people who refused to hear His voice that He would punish them by sending them a foreign nation whose language they did not know, the Assyrian and Babylonian nation, and yet they did not hear. The Apostle's purpose in quoting this verse is to show that the use of foreign languages does not make, and did not make, unbelievers believers or the disobedient obedient.

14.18.0.en: Foreign tongues are given as a sign for the ministry of preaching among unbelievers so that they may believe when they see it as a miracle, as happened on the day of Pentecost (Acts 2:1-15); they were amazed, then were convinced and believed when each of them understood what was said in his own language. As for believers, the better thing for them is the word of prophecy, which is the interpretation of the word of God and religious teaching by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit in the language of the hearers.

14.19.0.en: If the believers come together in the Church and all of them are speaking with tongues, and there come in unlearned persons, that is, believers who do not know these languages, or unbelievers, they will judge of them that they are raving or that they are mad.

14.20.0.en: But if there come into the Church those who do not know the languages, or Jews or pagans, merely to look on at new things, and they find one speaking who preaches and teaches and calls to repentance, his words will affect them and prick their hearts, for the speech will be like a judgment upon them, and prove to them that they are sinners and liable to eternal perdition.

14.21.0.en: Thus he is exposed before himself as guilty before God and devoid of all righteousness, and he falls down before God as a sign of his repentance and bears witness to the truth that he has believed, and that you are the children of God, led by the Holy Spirit who dwells in you.

14.21.1.en: May you be occupied with the salvation of the souls of others and not with showing your own abilities, so that your concern may be like that of your Master Jesus Christ; and do not be afraid to show the truth even if it pricks some hearts, taking care not to fall into judging, and let the firm speech be with gentleness and meekness.

14.22.s.en: (5) The regulation of the use of gifts

14.22.0.en: What ought to be done when you come together for the worship of God in the Church is to take care to direct your gifts to the edification of the souls of the hearers.

14.22.1.en: “Hath a psalm”: that is, the Holy Spirit inspires him to sing a psalm, chanting and praising with it to the glory of God. In this is an indication of the origin of the prayer of the Psalms and the use of the Agpeya.

14.22.2.en: “Hath a doctrine”: that is, he has the gift of teaching one of the doctrines.

14.22.3.en: “Hath a tongue”: that is, the Holy Spirit grants him to speak in a new language for preaching; another has a revelation from the Holy Spirit to prophesy about the future or to disclose one of the hidden mysteries; another has the gift of interpreting languages. So let all your work be for edification and the repentance of straying souls.

14.23.0.en: If anyone speaks in a foreign tongue, order is important in the use of this gift. The number of those speaking in a tongue must not exceed two or three at the most, and they must not speak at the same time but each in his turn, provided there is someone to interpret.

14.24.0.en: If there is no one to interpret, let no one speak in a foreign tongue inside the Church, but he may pray in it to God alone.

14.25.0.en: If there are prophets, that is, preachers, in the Church, not more than two or three should speak, each in his turn.

14.25.1.en: “The other”: that is, those who have the gift of discerning sound preaching from what is wrong or unprofitable; these must judge and direct those who have the gift of prophesying or teaching.

14.26.0.en: If the Holy Spirit guides someone to add or to teach a spiritual teaching, the first must keep silent so that the other can declare these words. Thus worship proceeds in order and arrangement, and two do not speak at the same time.

14.27.0.en: In sum, you can arrange the preaching one after another so that the hearers may benefit.

14.28.0.en: Here St. Paul affirms the preacher’s ability to speak when he wishes and to be silent when he wishes, so that each gives the other the opportunity without crowding or disturbance. The prophets who preach to the people have a will that controls their spirits and their speech; they are silent when they wish or speak according to need, and their spirits do not rob them of their will so that they find themselves launching into speech in spite of themselves; rather they are able to control themselves.

14.29.0.en: God, the giver of the gifts of prophecy, is a God of order and rejects chaos and disturbance. Accordingly order and peace must prevail in all the Christian churches everywhere, and each one must not crowd to show his gift, for this hides pride in the heart.

14.30.0.en: The Apostle holds that it is shameful for a woman to speak in the Church. By this limitation of the woman’s authority, the Apostle defined the functions that none but a man may exercise in the Church. The Church, for example, restricts some of its spiritual functions to men and not women, such as the priesthood, and the priest is a teacher.

14.30.1.en: This does not mean the superiority of man over woman in kind or creation, but we must not ignore that there are natural differences between man and woman that have an effect in defining the sphere of activity and work of each of them, as stated in the Book of Genesis concerning the woman’s subjection to the man (Gen 3:16). But a woman can teach women and children. The preceding discussion concerns speaking and teaching in the Church that gathers men and women, whether in the Liturgies or in general meetings.

14.31.0.en: A statement containing a rebuke of the Church of Corinth, because it seems they had departed from the orders of worship in the Church, so he wanted to alert them to the necessity of observing the Church’s order, which was established in accordance with the divine will. He asks them, with a kind of irony, whether your setting up strange orders in worship is due to your thinking that you are the origin of the preaching of the Gospel, or whether the right to arrange the worship of the Church belongs to you alone?!

14.32.0.en: If anyone reckons himself a prophet or that he has received spiritual gifts, let him know that what I instruct you is from the Lord. For Paul, as an Apostle, has authority from God to establish an order of worship in the Church, and a person cannot be a Christian called by God and have true spiritual gifts and yet refuse to hear His apostle and obey him.

14.32.1.en: This is a lesson for us. If a teacher claims to be sent by God and that we must obey him, we must compare his teaching with the teaching of the Holy Bible, and if it does not agree with it, we are certain that he is not from God.

14.33.0.en: If anyone wishes to ignore what I instruct you, let him bear the responsibility for this ignoring. In this he clears his responsibility as an apostle who instructed them by the Spirit, while the responsibility of acceptance and obedience rests on them alone; that is, whoever obeys, obeys, and whoever does not obey is rejecting God’s teachings and will be judged.

14.34.0.en: All the discourse of this chapter is about the two gifts mentioned, namely prophesying, that is, preaching, and speaking in tongues. This verse is the summary, which is that the first is better than the second and a Christian ought to desire it and be diligent in seeking it, and that the use of the second in the Church must not be prevented, because it too is profitable, on condition that there is someone to interpret so that the hearers may benefit.

14.35.0.en: All matters of worship must be done with order and concord in all the churches, and everything must be within the bounds of decency and according to the order established for communal worship. It is not right for an individual or a local church to deviate from the rest of the individuals and churches.

14.35.1.en: Take care to obey the teachings of the Church and the guidance of your father of confession, and if you want to add anything in your service, let it be with the approval of those in charge, so that it does not conflict with the order of the Church. The more you humble yourself, the easier it is for you to obey and to concentrate on the salvation of your soul and the love of God.

14.35.2.en: A reply to the heresy of denying the resurrection of bodies
